title: Simchat Torah, lived
hookLine: dancing with the scroll, even if you don't know the steps
tomorrow: a month with no holidays at all. now what?

lines: THE BOOK ENDS AND STARTS OVER.
cards: Weddings have this moment: the music changes, a circle forms, and the uncle who swears he can't dance gets pulled in anyway. Simchat Torah has the same moment, with a Torah scroll in the middle of the circle.
The last lines of Deuteronomy are read, and then, right away, the first lines of Genesis. The book ends and starts over in the same breath, and so does the dancing.

teach.b: Simchat Torah means the joy of the Torah.

The scrolls come out of the ark and are carried around the room in circles called hakafot, with singing, kids on shoulders, and plenty of people who have no idea what the steps are. Nobody's checking.
When David brought the ark of God up to Jerusalem, the text says, "David danced before the LORD with all his might."
With all his might, not with all his skill. So: dance anyway. And since the circle starts over today, walk back around the one we just made.
Hear every note: the commandment of the shofar is listening.
Ten small changes: the window between the holy days. Life comes first: when the fast puts someone at risk, eating is the commandment. The last hour: Neilah, the gates locking, one long note.
A small hut is enough: open sky and a little table. Guests in the booth: the ancestors' seat goes to someone in need. Six lines, one season of holy days, and now the book begins again.

how: On Simchat Torah, congregations take every Torah scroll out of the ark and dance with them in circles (hakafot), then read the end of Deuteronomy and the beginning of Genesis; children often get flags and treats.

the book and the circle start over together.
David danced before the ark with careful, dignified steps

games.q: your cousin, at her first Simchat Torah, freezes at the edge of the circle: 'i don't know what to do.' what's the answer?
o: watch this year and learn the steps for next time.
jump in and move; nobody's checking the steps.
hold a scroll on the side so you don't have to dance.
games.why: the joy is the point here. David danced with all his might, not with all his skill.

practice: For the sit, let your body move a little, standing or seated. Sway side to side, slowly, the way a crowd sways when it's carrying something it loves. There are no steps to get right.
If a tune comes to mind, hum it under your breath and let it set the pace.
